entries.place: Gravel drive outside the Redmist Estate gate
entries.what_happened: Carla introduced herself as Julian's bodyguard, said his safety was her top priority, and asked to borrow his phone. Julian gave his name and asked what she would do with it. She said she would run a threat assessment — contacts, accounts, anything exposed — with nothing deleted and nothing leaving her hands, and he could watch. Julian kept the phone in his own hand and unlocked only what she needed. In the login history they found an entry from three days before, after Julian booked his train, from somewhere near the estate; Julian said he had told no one but his mother he was coming. Carla told him not to clear the history and explained the master key: one passcode Bernard held that opens every estate lock, accounts, foundation books, vault and doors, now due to pass to Julian through a procedure run by Jezebel with the lawyer as witness. She said the login suggested someone knew the handoff was coming and that the procedure might be compromised.

entries.place: Gatehouse, then the mansion's marble hallway
entries.what_happened: Julian asked how the procedure could be compromised and whether Jezebel knew of the login. Carla said Jezebel did not know yet and that the login would stay between them for a day; she trusted Jezebel but considered the room, witnesses and lawyer suspect. In the gatehouse, which smelled of coffee and gun oil and had monitors showing the drive, rear service road and pier gate, they agreed to ask Jezebel straight about the procedure while letting her think Julian's concern was an heir's nerves. Carla said Jezebel's office was in the east wing. They crossed the gravel and entered the mansion by a side door. Julian said he would listen and not interrupt during the walkthrough, and that Carla should speak if a step did not match what she remembered; she agreed.

entries.place: Marble hallway of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Gabriella came out of a door ahead of them in a lavender gown and pearls, said she had waited since seven, and offered to show Julian the house, calling Carla his minder. Carla greeted her and kept walking. Julian thanked Gabriella but declined, saying he had business with Jezebel about finances and paperwork first and would walk the house later on his own time. Gabriella's smile went brittle; she warned him the east wing had a draft nobody had fixed and said she would be in the west parlor that afternoon if the paperwork spared him, then went back upstairs. Carla told Julian there was no draft in the east wing and that it was a warning to keep him away from something. Julian said it could be a lure, that they would not investigate today, and that after Jezebel he wanted to learn what Gabriella did not want him to see.

entries.place: Jezebel's office in the east wing
entries.what_happened: Julian knocked and Jezebel let him and Carla in. Julian asked to understand the accounts and foundations and to see the master-key handoff end to end before setting a new code, presenting himself as a worried new heir. Jezebel described the handoff: the vault room off the old dispensary, lawyer Campion and Jezebel as witnesses, a sealed slip only Bernard read, destroyed once the new code is set, an hour in all. Asked who told him, Julian said an old friend of Bernard's. Pressed on the slip, Jezebel recalled a retired locksmith who serviced the mechanism four years before with the door propped open and the slip in hand, a visit she had signed off on. She asked what he feared in that room. Julian revealed the login three days earlier, before he had told anyone in Islaport he was coming, and asked whom Bernard would have trusted with knowledge of the key. Jezebel named Bernard's dead brother Edmund, Campion, and Marguerite, Bernard's nurse of his last two years, then said Bernard wrote everything down in a log in the bottom drawer of his private desk in the study, which she had never opened and said he should not open without cause — but that he might have cause now.
